draft.title: Change and continuity in China
card: Change is something that was different by 1976 from how it was in 1912. Continuity is something that stayed much the same over that time.
landlords and the old elite lost their power. Land reform in the early 1950s took land from landlords and gave it to peasants.
China was still ruled without free elections or open opposition. Power stayed in the hands of one party, and ordinary people still faced hardship.
Hardship took different forms. Before 1949 it came from war, poverty and unrest. After 1949 campaigns, the famine of the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution brought suffering to many.
draft.remember: The old elite lost power, but strong central rule and hardship for many carried on.

a.q: Which of these is a change in China between 1912 and 1976?
opts: Landlords lost their land and their power
Power stayed in the hands of one party
Many ordinary people still faced hardship
Rulers still used force against opponents
a.why: Land reform took land from landlords, so the old elite no longer held power. The other options describe things that stayed the same, so they are continuities. One-party rule is the tempting one, but it carried on rather than changed.
a.clue: Which group was in a different position by 1976?

b.q: A student says the 1949 revolution changed everything for ordinary Chinese people. Which fact from the 1950s to 1970s best shows continuity?
opts: Many people still suffered hardship under new rulers
Peasants received land that had belonged to landlords
Landlords no longer held power in their villages
Old elites lost their place at the top of society
b.why: Many people still suffered, in new ways such as the famine after the Great Leap Forward. This shows hardship continued even though rulers changed. The land given to peasants is the tempting option, but it is a change, not a continuity.
b.clue: Look for what stayed the same, not what was new.

a.best: Landlords lost their land and their power

b.best: Many people still suffered hardship under new rulers

problems.detail: The card says power 'stayed in the hands of one party' and China was 'still ruled without free elections' from 1912. In 1912–13 the new Republic held national elections contested by several parties. From 1916 to 1928 warlords divided China. One-party Guomindang rule only began around 1928, so one-party rule did not run continuously from 1912.

'Strong central rule ... carried on' is false for much of 1912–1949, when China was split by warlords, civil war and Japanese invasion. The card also says nothing about strong central rule, so the remember line claims more than the card teaches.
Land reform belongs to point 1. The card explains what it did ('took land from landlords and gave it to peasants') instead of only mentioning it.
The right option is the only one containing 'still', which signals continuity. A student could pick it without understanding the idea.
The three wrong options all contain 'still' or 'stayed', and the right option is the only one without such a word. This cue gives the answer away.

check.summary: The card and remember line wrongly treat one-party, strong central rule as continuous from 1912, ignoring the 1912–13 elections, the warlord era and the civil war. Both questions can be answered from the word 'still' rather than from understanding change and continuity.

proposal.title: Change and continuity in China
card: Change is what was different in 1976 from how it was in 1912. Continuity is what stayed much the same, even if its form shifted.
the Qing emperor gave up the throne in 1912. By the 1950s landlords and the old gentry elite had also lost their power, through land reform and other campaigns.
for most of the period, rulers did not allow open opposition. Warlords divided China from 1916 to 1928, the Guomindang ran a one-party state from 1928, and the Communist Party did from 1949.
Hardship for many also carried on in new forms. Before 1949 it came from war, poverty and unrest. After 1949 it came from campaigns, the famine of the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution.
proposal.remember: The old elite lost power, but rule without open opposition and hardship for many carried on for most of the period.

a.q: Which of these is a change between 1912 and 1976, not a continuity?
opts: Landlords and the gentry lost their power in the villages
Many ordinary people faced hunger, poverty and violence
Rulers put down open opposition to their rule
Ordinary people had little say in who ruled them
a.why: Landlords and the gentry held power in 1912 but had lost it by the 1950s, so their position was different. The other three describe things found under warlords, the Guomindang and the Communist Party alike. Little say in who ruled is tempting because rulers changed, but people's lack of a say did not.
a.clue: Which group was in a very different position by 1976?

b.q: A student says the 1949 revolution changed everything for ordinary Chinese people. Which fact from the 1950s to 1970s best shows continuity?
opts: Millions died in the famine after the Great Leap Forward
Peasants were given land taken from landlords
Landlords no longer ran life in the villages
Old gentry families lost their place in society
b.why: Hunger and suffering were common before 1949, and the famine shows they carried on in a new form after it. Peasants getting land is tempting because it affected ordinary people, but it was something new, so it is a change.
b.clue: Which fact describes something people also faced before 1949?

a.best: Landlords and the gentry lost their power in the villages

b.best: Millions died in the famine after the Great Leap Forward

problems.detail: The right option stands out. The other three options all restate the same change (landlords and gentry losing power, peasants gaining land), so a student can pick the famine as the odd one out without understanding continuity.

'The famine after the Great Leap Forward' suggests the famine came once the campaign was over. It happened during it (about 1959 to 1961), and the card itself says 'the famine of the Great Leap Forward'.

check.summary: The facts and the answers to both questions are sound. In question b the right option stands out because the three distractors all say the same thing about landlords, and 'after the Great Leap Forward' should read 'during' or 'of' it.
